user: I'm CUS-0004. Transaction TX-0401, 240.00 EUR: the goods never arrived. Which reason code applies?
answer:
The reason code for a goods that never arrived is **goods_not_received**.

Under Verta's dispute rules, this code has a **90-day window counted from the transaction date**. A dispute opened after that window closes is not eligible. I haven't checked TX-0401's date yet, so I can't confirm it is still within the window.

Your account is ACC-1005 (EUR, balance 1,310.20).

If you want to proceed, I'll first check TX-0401's eligibility under this code. I'll open the dispute only if that check passes, and I'll confirm with you before filing. Would you like me to do that?

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Notifications
## Dispute updates
A dispute generates a notification on every state change. The notification
names the state, never the internal reason for a decision.
